Coleman Snap N Go vs YETI Roadie 15: Best Hard Cooler for Day Trips?

The world's first collapsible hard cooler ($153.99) takes on the rotomolded legend ($200) — and the answer isn't as obvious as you'd think.

Updated July 2026 · Outdoor & Camping · 8 min read

The Quick Take

Two very different approaches to the same problem: keeping your drinks and food cold while you're out for the day. The Coleman Snap N Go 45qt is a groundbreaking new design — a hard-sided cooler that collapses to one-third its size when empty. The YETI Roadie 15 is a miniaturized version of YETI's legendary rotomolded coolers — built like a tank, keeps ice for days, and costs a premium.

These coolers target different buyers, but one of them delivers dramatically better value for most people.

Our Pick Coleman Snap N Go 45qt Collapsible Hard Cooler

The Coleman Snap N Go is a genuine innovation — the first hard cooler that doesn't monopolize closet space when you're not using it. It collapses to one-third its size in seconds, holds 76 cans, keeps ice cold for 55 hours, and supports up to 200 lbs. At $153.99, it matches YETI's practicality for day trips while adding a storage-friendly design the Roadie can't touch.

The Storage Problem That Coleman Solved

Hard coolers have one major drawback: when they're empty, they still take up the same amount of space. A YETI Tundra 45 takes up a corner of your garage 365 days a year, even though you only use it 10-15 times. The Coleman Snap N Go addresses this directly. When you're done, you press a button, it collapses to ⅓ of its size, and slides into a cabinet, under a bed, or behind a car seat.

This matters for apartment dwellers, RV owners, and anyone who doesn't have a dedicated "cooler corner" in their garage. The Snap N Go stores flat — roughly the size of a large briefcase — and sets up in less than 10 seconds.

Ice Retention — The YETI's Strong Suit

Let's be fair to YETI: rotomolded construction is the gold standard for ice retention. The Roadie 15 can keep ice cold for 3-5 days in moderate conditions, and even longer if you pre-chill and use block ice. The Coleman Snap N Go manages a respectable 55 hours — more than enough for a weekend camping trip or a long day at the beach, but not in the same league as YETI for extended off-grid adventures.

That said, for 90% of cooler uses — day trips, beach days, tailgates, picnics — 55 hours is overkill in the right direction. You'd never run out of cold drinks in a single day with either cooler.

Capacity — Not Even Close

The Coleman holds 76 cans without ice — roughly 4x the YETI Roadie 15's capacity of about 18 cans with ice. That's a whole different class of utility. The Coleman fits a full case of beer plus a bag of ice, with room for lunch. The YETI Roadie handles a six-pack, a few sandwiches, and some ice.

If you're tailgating, feeding a family at the beach, or packing for a group, the Coleman's size advantage is overwhelming. The YETI Roadie is best as a personal cooler for one or two people.

Build Quality & Practicality

The Coleman's collapsible design uses a rigid polypropylene structure with a fully insulated lid and body, plus a removable waterproof liner for easy cleaning. When it's assembled, it feels as solid as a traditional cooler. The latches are sturdy, the carry handles are comfortable, and it can support up to 200 lbs — you can sit on it or use it as a side table at a campsite.

The YETI Roadie 15 is built to military-grade rotomolded standards. It's virtually indestructible — you could drop it off a truck bed and it would be fine. The DoubleDuty shoulder strap is comfortable, the T-Rex lid latches are famously tough, and the Bearfoot non-slip feet keep it planted. But all that durability comes with a weight penalty and zero flexibility for storage.

Who Should Buy Each?

Buy the Coleman Snap N Go if: You want a family-sized cooler for day trips, you have limited storage space, you appreciate innovative design, and you want the best value for your money. At $153.99, it's a cooler that genuinely solves problems.

Buy the YETI Roadie 15 if: You need extreme ice retention for multi-day trips, you want an indestructible cooler that will last a decade, you value brand cachet, and capacity isn't your primary concern.

Final Verdict

Our Pick Coleman Snap N Go 45qt

More capacity, innovative collapsible design, excellent ice retention for day trips, and $46 cheaper than the YETI. This is the cooler most people should buy — it stores small but performs big.

FAQ

Does the Coleman Snap N Go leak?
No — the removable liner is fully waterproof, and the insulated body is leakproof when fully assembled. The company explicitly markets it as leakproof.

Can I use the YETI Roadie as a seat?
Yes — the Roadie 15 is strong enough to sit on. The Coleman can also support up to 200 lbs, making both usable as auxiliary seating.

How long does the Coleman take to collapse?
Under 10 seconds. Press the release, fold the sides, and it flattens. To set up, just pull it open until it snaps into place.

Which is better for car camping?
The Coleman's size and collapsibility make it ideal for car camping — you can pack it flat when empty. The YETI is better for extended off-grid trips where ice retention matters most.
